source.description:
PROBLEM
The picker shows specialist panes/sessions but not who dispatched them. Today `sp-*` sessions are pulled into a flat `── specialists (sp-*) ──` section (bin/tmux-session-picker:3719-3720, header at :3889) and a pane row carries the dispatcher only as a `from:<parent>` meta token (agent_meta_label, :532).

The lineage edge already exists on the specialist's own pane: `@agent_parent_session` (tmux session id, never recycled) and `@agent_parent_pane`. It is written by the core launcher — core/cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts:1991 and codex-worktree-session.ts:334, driven by the `--role`/`--parent` options on `xt pi` / `xt claude` — and asserted by core/test/integration-suite/suite-c-coordinator-lineage.mjs:308.

The picker already READS both fields (list format at bin/tmux-session-picker:517, topology format at :2059, projection keys at :744-747) but uses them only for that label. So the information is present and unread: a dispatcher cannot see at a glance which of its dispatched specialists are active, or what state they are in.

SUCCESS
- A specialist carrying a lineage edge renders as a child of the dispatching pane's row, one level deeper, in the same list, with no separate section.
- The child row states exactly: specialist, role, lifecycle state (existing `[sp]` badge + state badge + bead). Nothing more.
- Missing lineage is handled explicitly: a specialist with no edge, or whose parent is not currently in the list, still appears (orphan bucket) and never vanishes.
- Filtering/modes never hide a child silently while its parent is shown.

SCOPE
Step 0 - prerequisite, gates the whole requirement: inventory whether the launched specialist pane actually carries the edge, per dispatch surface.
  (a) pi subagents extension: ~/dev/specialists/config/pi-extensions/specialist-subagents/index.mjs
  (b) claude plugin: ~/dev/specialists/plugins/specialists/ (hooks + scripts/mcp-server.mjs)
  (c) legacy CLI: `sp` -> dist/index.js, tmux creation in src/cli/tmux-utils.ts
  Verified so far: none of the three writes the edge in its own source, and tmux-utils.ts has no agent option stamping at all; the only writers found are core's two worktree-session launchers. Any surface that does not route through that launcher needs a writer (its own item in the owning repo) or is out of coverage - the inventory must say which.
Step 1 - xtmux: grouping and indentation in build_list (bin/tmux-session-picker), reusing the already-read fields. The `sp-*` section becomes the orphan bucket.

NON_GOALS
- Progress, percent, elapsed, ETA, streamed output, log tail. The requirement is "active and what state", nothing else.
- Dispatch control (pause/kill/retry/reconnect) and any state write by the picker.
- Changing how specialists dispatch, except where Step 0 proves a writer is missing - that is its own item in the owning repo.
- The nav card renderer and the topology JSON projection: they already carry parent ids; extending them is separate.
- Headless specialists with no tmux pane: there is nothing to nest.

CONSTRAINTS
- Row TSV stays 5 fields - test/contract.sh asserts exactly 4 tabs per row.
- Attribute-only emphasis, colour stays the fzf palette's.
- A child stays attached to its parent under the existing attention/state sort, so a parent that sorts late still carries its children; ordering within a parent's child group must be stable across renders.
- Cycle and self guard: a parent chain that loops, or a parent that is the pane itself, renders at top level.
- Parent preference: @agent_parent_pane when set, else @agent_parent_session. Both are stable tmux ids.
- A dead or absent parent is an orphan, not an error and not a hidden row.

VALIDATION
- Fixture-driven: extend the fake-core contract tests (tests/contracts/classic-picker-ui.test.ts pattern) with hand-built lineage rows - child with pane parent, child with session-only parent, absent parent, self-parent, cycle - and assert the rendered tree and row order.
- Render capture in an isolated tmux server (pattern already used for the picker work) showing a synthetic two-level tree with indent and badges.
- One real dispatch per surface Step 0 names: read the pane options back and confirm the row lands under its dispatcher.

OUTPUT
Step 0's inventory (which surfaces carry the edge, which need a writer), then the display change with the tests above. Draft until Step 0 is answered: without a lineage edge on the specialist pane, indentation renders nothing.
source.notes:
Cross-repo counterpart filed 2026-09-12 in the specialists repo: unitAI-vc7tl - 'specialist launches must stamp the dispatching pane's lineage (@agent_parent_session / @agent_parent_pane)', P2, external-ref bead:xtmux-oj2. That bead owns Step 0 (the per-surface inventory) and the missing writers; this bead owns the display side only. Verified when filing it: none of the three surfaces (subagents pi extension, claude plugin, legacy CLI tmux-utils.ts) writes the edge in its own source; the only writers anywhere are core/cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts:1991 and codex-worktree-session.ts:334. Relevant precedent found on that board: unitAI-pcso (reuse surface for xt worktree-session.ts) and unitAI-umtck (already consumes the coordinator's @agent_branch).
CONSUMER CONSEQUENCE for the native dispatch path (2026-09-13, operator requires native coverage too): a native in-process activation has NO tmux pane (verified: config/pi-extensions/specialist-subagents/index.mjs never calls tmux), so there is no pane row to nest and no child-pane option to read. The display therefore needs a second source, and the choice belongs with the specialists-side design (recorded on unitAI-vc7tl): either (i) the native runtime's Fleet Registry carries dispatcher {tmux_session_id, tmux_pane_id, agent_instance_id} and the picker reads the registry, or (ii) the dispatcher's own pane carries a small option (e.g. @agent_native_activations) listing its live native children, which keeps the picker on the existing tmux-option path. Option (ii) means the nesting code has two inputs (parent_pane on the child, plus a dispatcher-side list) rather than one; option (i) means the picker gains a runtime query. Either way the row must render the same shape: role + lifecycle state, nested under the dispatcher.
XTRM-96 BOUNDARY (Jira 'Specialists observability vNext'; same workstream, found 2026-09-13). That ticket requires the same feature - parent/child nesting under the agent that called the specialist, for CLI, native Pi and MCP dispatches - but mandates the mechanism for ITS surfaces: 'The fleet tree must use durable forensic lineage, not tmux heuristics' (job.started + correlation.parent_job_id + links.spawned_by.kind -> runtime-origin-reconstruct.ts reconstructLineage() -> FleetTree), and 'Do not copy the picker's process-tree/session-name detection into Specialists'.

Consequence for this bead: nesting in the xtmux picker reads the tmux options (@agent_parent_pane / @agent_parent_session) - which is correct FOR THE PICKER, since tmux options are its native source and the specialists side now stamps them (unitAI-vc7tl, PR #383). But this must never be presented as, or reused as, the Specialists fleet tree's lineage source; that is XTRM-96's reconstructLineage over observability.db. Two consumers, two sources, one vocabulary.
source.title: scope: nest dispatched specialists under their dispatching pane (active + status only)
